question:
The following sentence has been divided into three segments. One of them may contain an adverbial usage error. Select the option that has the segment with the error. If you don’t find any error, select ‘No error’ as your answer.
Mrs. Arunima / speaks / Telugu well.
options: speaks
Mrs. Arunima
Telugu well.
No error
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "No error"


Explanation:

☛The given sentence "Mrs. Arunima / speaks / Telugu well." has no error.
☛"Mrs. Arunima" - This is a noun and the subject of the sentence, which is correct.
☛"speaks" - This is a verb and is used correctly in the sentence.
☛"Telugu well" - Here, "Telugu" is a noun and "well" is an adverb modifying the verb "speaks," which is grammatically correct.
☛Thus, all parts of the sentence are correct, and there is no error.



Grammar Rules:

☛Adverb: An adverb modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb. It tells how, when, where, or to what extent an action is performed.
☛Adverb of Manner: "Well" is an adverb of manner that describes how the action is performed. Here, it describes how Mrs. Arunima speaks Telugu.
☛Subject-Verb Agreement: The subject ("Mrs. Arunima") and verb ("speaks") agree correctly in the sentence.



Example:
InCorrect - She speaks Telugu good. (Incorrect because "good" is an adjective and cannot modify a verb.)

Correct - She speaks Telugu well. (Correct because "well" is an adverb modifying the verb "speaks.")
question_hi:

Mrs. Arunima / speaks / Telugu well.
options_hi: speaks
Mrs. Arunima
Telugu well.
No error
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "No error"


Explanation:

☛दिए गए वाक्य "Mrs. Arunima / speaks / Telugu well." में कोई त्रुटि नहीं है।
☛"Mrs. Arunima" - यह संज्ञा (noun) है और वाक्य का subject है, जो सही है।
☛"speaks" - यह क्रिया (verb) है और यह सही रूप में प्रयुक्त हुई है।
☛"Telugu well" - यहाँ "Telugu" संज्ञा (noun) है और "well" क्रिया-विशेषण (adverb) है जो क्रिया "speaks" को modify कर रहा है, जो व्याकरणिक रूप से सही है।
☛इस प्रकार, वाक्य के सभी भाग सही हैं और कोई त्रुटि नहीं है।



Grammar Rules:

☛Adverb: एक adverb एक क्रिया, विशेषण, या दूसरे adverb को modify करता है। यह बताता है कि क्रिया कैसे, कब, कहाँ, या किस हद तक की गई है।
☛Adverb of Manner: "Well" एक adverb of manner है जो बताता है कि क्रिया कैसे की गई है। यहाँ यह बताता है कि Mrs. Arunima Telugu कैसे बोलती हैं।
☛Subject-Verb Agreement: वाक्य में subject ("Mrs. Arunima") और verb ("speaks") का agreement सही है।



Example:
InCorrect - She speaks Telugu good. (गलत क्योंकि "good" एक adjective है जो क्रिया को modify नहीं कर सकता।)

Correct - She speaks Telugu well. (सही क्योंकि "well" एक adverb है जो क्रिया "speaks" को modify करता है।)

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
If it will rain tomorrow, I will stay at home.
options: I will
at home
will rain
If it
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "will rain"


Explanation:

☛The error in the given sentence lies in the part "If it will rain tomorrow".
☛In English grammar, we do not use future tense (will/shall) after "If" in conditional sentences.
☛For Type 1 Conditional Sentences, we use Simple Present Tense in the "If" clause and Future Tense (will/shall) in the main clause.
☛The correct sentence should be: "If it rains tomorrow, I will stay at home."



Grammar Rules:

☛Conditional Sentences (Type 1): These sentences express real and possible conditions.
☛Structure: If + Simple Present, will/shall + V1 (Main Verb)
☛Example: If you study well, you will pass the exam.
☛Note: Using future tense in the "If" clause is a common mistake often tested in exams.



Example:
InCorrect - If it will rain, we will cancel the trip.

Correct - If it rains, we will cancel the trip.

Example:
InCorrect - If it will rain, we will cancel the trip.

Correct - If it rains, we will cancel the trip.

question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error.
He organises / a children’s fair every year / and his friends comes / to attend it.
options: He organises
a children’s fair every year
to attend it.
and his friends comes
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "and his friends comes"


Explanation:

☛The segment "and his friends comes" contains a grammatical error.
☛"Friends" is a plural noun, so it should be paired with the plural verb "come", not the singular verb "comes".
☛The correct phrase should be: "and his friends come".
☛According to the Subject-Verb Agreement rule, a plural subject must take a plural verb.



Grammar Rules:

☛Subject-Verb Agreement: The verb must always agree with its subject in number (singular/plural) and person (first, second, third).
☛Use plural verbs (come, go, are) with plural subjects (e.g., friends, children, books).
☛Use singular verbs (comes, goes, is) with singular subjects (e.g., friend, child, book).



Example:
InCorrect - She and her brother goes to school.

Correct - She and her brother go to school.
question_hi:

Explanation:

☛"Friends" एक बहुवचन संज्ञा (plural noun) है, इसलिए इसके साथ बहुवचन क्रिया (plural verb) "come" का प्रयोग होना चाहिए, न कि एकवचन क्रिया (singular verb) "comes" का।
☛सही वाक्यांश होगा: "and his friends come"।
☛Subject-Verb Agreement के नियम के अनुसार, बहुवचन subject के साथ बहुवचन verb का प्रयोग किया जाता है।



Grammar Rules:

☛Subject-Verb Agreement: क्रिया (verb) हमेशा अपने subject के number (एकवचन/बहुवचन) और person (प्रथम, द्वितीय, तृतीय) के अनुसार होनी चाहिए।
☛बहुवचन subject (जैसे friends, children, books) के साथ बहुवचन क्रिया (come, go, are) का प्रयोग करें।
☛एकवचन subject (जैसे friend, child, book) के साथ एकवचन क्रिया (comes, goes, is) का प्रयोग करें।



Example:
InCorrect - She and her brother goes to school.

Correct - She and her brother go to school.

question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error.
He do not / fear the / repercussions of / this decision.
options: repercussions of
this decision.
He do not
fear the
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "He do not"


Explanation:

☛The segment "He do not" contains a grammatical error in the given sentence.
☛With the subject "He" (third person singular), the auxiliary verb "does" should be used instead of "do".
☛The correct sentence should be: "He does not fear the repercussions of this decision."
☛In Present Indefinite Tense, third person singular subjects (He, She, It) require the verb to have 's'/'es' suffix or use of "does" as auxiliary verb.



Grammar Rules:

☛Subject-Verb Agreement: Singular subjects take singular verbs and plural subjects take plural verbs.
☛Present Indefinite Tense: For third person singular subjects, either add 's'/'es' to main verb or use "does" as auxiliary verb.
☛In negative sentences, use "does not" (doesn't) or "do not" (don't) according to the subject.



Example:
InCorrect - She do not play tennis.

Correct - She does not play tennis.

solution_hi:

Explanation:

☛दिए गए वाक्य में "He do not" में व्याकरणिक त्रुटि है।
☛Subject "He" (third person singular) के साथ auxiliary verb "does" का प्रयोग होना चाहिए, न कि "do"।
☛सही वाक्य होगा: "He does not fear the repercussions of this decision."
☛Present Indefinite Tense में third person singular subject (He, She, It) के साथ verb में 's'/'es' जोड़ा जाता है या "does" का प्रयोग किया जाता है।



Grammar Rules:

☛Subject-Verb Agreement: Singular subject के साथ singular verb और plural subject के साथ plural verb का प्रयोग होता है।
☛Present Indefinite Tense: Third person singular subject के साथ main verb में 's'/'es' जोड़ा जाता है या auxiliary verb "does" का प्रयोग किया जाता है।
☛Negative sentences में "does not" (doesn't) या "do not" (don't) का प्रयोग subject के अनुसार किया जाता है।



Example:
InCorrect - He do not like apples.

Correct - He does not like apples.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
I had seen / her with her mother / in the cinema hall / yesterday.
options: in the cinema hall
her with her mother
yesterday
I had seen
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "I had seen"

Explanation:
☛ The segment "I had seen" is incorrect because it uses the Past Perfect Tense inappropriately.
☛ The Past Perfect Tense (had + past participle) is used to describe an action that was completed before another action in the past. However, in this sentence, there is only one action, and the time indicator "yesterday" suggests the use of Simple Past Tense.
☛ The correct sentence should be: "I saw her with her mother in the cinema hall yesterday."

Grammar Rules:
☛ The Past Perfect Tense (Subject + had + V3) is used for an action that was completed before another past action.
☛ The Simple Past Tense (Subject + V2) is used for actions that occurred at a specific time in the past.
☛ Time markers like yesterday, last night, ago usually require the Simple Past Tense.

Example:
InCorrect - I had seen her yesterday.
Correct - I saw her yesterday.
question_hi:

I had seen / her with her mother / in the cinema hall / yesterday.
options_hi: in the cinema hall
her with her mother
yesterday
I had seen
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "I had seen"

Explanation:
☛ दिए गए वाक्य में "I had seen" गलत है क्योंकि यहाँ Past Perfect Tense का गलत प्रयोग हुआ है।
☛ Past Perfect Tense का उपयोग तब किया जाता है जब एक क्रिया दूसरी क्रिया से पहले पूरी हो चुकी हो, लेकिन यहाँ केवल एक ही क्रिया है और समय सूचक शब्द "yesterday" है जो Simple Past Tense का संकेत देता है।
☛ सही वाक्य होगा: "I saw her with her mother in the cinema hall yesterday."

Grammar Rules:
☛ Past Perfect Tense (Subject + had + V3) का प्रयोग दो क्रियाओं में से पहले घटित होने वाली क्रिया के लिए किया जाता है।
☛ Simple Past Tense (Subject + V2) का प्रयोग उन क्रियाओं के लिए किया जाता है जो अतीत में एक निश्चित समय पर घटित हुई हों।
☛ यदि वाक्य में yesterday, last night, ago जैसे समय सूचक शब्द हों तो Simple Past Tense का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।

Example:
InCorrect - I had seen her yesterday.
Correct - I saw her yesterday.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
In this cold weather, / there’s nothing / like good / cup of coffee.
options:
In this cold weather

like good

cup of coffee

there’s nothing
solution:
The error is in segment 2 — “like good”.

Explanation:

The phrase “a good cup of coffee” needs an article ('a') before “good”.
The correct sentence should be:

“In this cold weather, there’s nothing like a good cup of coffee.”

Grammar point:

  • Countable singular nouns (like cup) need an article (“a” or “the”) or another determiner before them.

  • Here, “cup” is singular and countable, so we must say “a cup”, not just “cup”.

Corrected sentence: In this cold weather, there’s nothing like a good cup of coffee.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
Today she said to her friend, “You’re the sweetest person I have met ever”.
options: I have met ever”.
her friend, “You’re
Today she said to
the sweetest person
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "I have met ever”."


Explanation:
☛ The error in the given sentence lies in the phrase "I have met ever” because the placement of 'ever' is incorrect.
☛ The correct sentence structure should be: "I have ever met" or "I have met you ever".
☛ 'Ever' is an adverb that usually comes after the main verb, but in this case, it should follow 'met'.
☛ In Present Perfect Tense (have met), 'ever' is used to denote experience, but its placement is wrong here.


Grammar Rules:
☛ Adverbs of time like 'ever', 'never', 'always' generally come between the auxiliary verb and the main verb.
☛ In Present Perfect Tense, the structure is 'have/has + past participle', and adverbs are placed between them.
☛ 'Ever' is more commonly used in questions and negative sentences; in positive sentences, 'always' or other adverbs are preferred.


Example:
InCorrect - "I have met ever”
Correct - "I have ever met" or "I have met you ever

☛ सही वाक्य संरचना होनी चाहिए: "I have ever met" या "I have met you ever"।
☛ 'Ever' एक adverb है जो आमतौर पर main verb के बाद आता है, लेकिन इस मामले में यह 'met' के बाद आना चाहिए था।
☛ Present Perfect Tense (have met) में 'ever' का प्रयोग अनुभव दर्शाने के लिए किया जाता है, लेकिन इसका स्थान गलत है।


Grammar Rules:
☛ Adverbs of time like 'ever', 'never', 'always' आमतौर पर main verb और auxiliary verb के बीच आते हैं।
☛ Present Perfect Tense में 'have/has + past participle' के बीच adverb रखा जाता है।
☛ 'Ever' का प्रयोग प्रश्नों और नकारात्मक वाक्यों में अधिक होता है, सकारात्मक वाक्यों में 'always' या अन्य adverbs प्रयोग किए जाते हैं।

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
The teacher was / taken back by / the audacity of / the new student.
A B C D
options: D
C
A
B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "B"


Explanation:
☛ Segment B contains the error with the phrase "taken back by".
☛ The correct phrase should be "taken aback by", which means 'surprised or shocked'.
☛ "Taken back" means 'to withdraw or retrieve', which is contextually incorrect here.
☛ "Taken aback" is a fixed idiom used to express surprise or astonishment.
☛ In this context, the teacher was surprised by the new student's audacity, making "taken aback" the appropriate choice.


Grammar Rules:
☛ Idioms and Phrases: English has many fixed idioms whose meanings can't be deduced from individual words. They must be used as-is.
☛ Phrasal Verbs: Prepositions in phrasal verbs are crucial. Changing them alters the meaning entirely.
☛ Contextual Meaning: Word choice must match the context. "Taken back" and "taken aback" have different meanings.


Example:
InCorrect - The teacher was taken back by the student's behavior.
Correct - The teacher was taken aback by the student's behavior.
question_hi:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
The teacher was / taken back by / the audacity of / the new student.
A B C D
options_hi: D
C
A
B
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "B"


Explanation:
☛ वाक्य के खंड B में "taken back by" गलत है।
☛ सही वाक्यांश "taken aback by" होना चाहिए, जिसका अर्थ है 'हैरान होना'।
☛ "Taken back" का अर्थ होता है 'वापस लेना', जो यहाँ संदर्भ के अनुसार सही नहीं है।
☛ "Taken aback" एक स्थिर मुहावरा (idiom) है जो आश्चर्य या हैरानी को व्यक्त करता है।
☛ यहाँ शिक्षक नए छात्र की धृष्टता से हैरान थे, इसलिए "taken aback" सही विकल्प है।


Grammar Rules:
☛ Idioms and Phrases: अंग्रेजी में कई स्थिर मुहावरे होते हैं जिनका अर्थ अलग होता है। इन्हें बदला नहीं जा सकता।
☛ Phrasal Verbs: कुछ वाक्यांशों में preposition का बहुत महत्व होता है। गलत preposition का प्रयोग अर्थ बदल देता है।
☛ Contextual Meaning: शब्दों का चयन संदर्भ के अनुसार होना चाहिए। "Taken back" और "taken aback" के अर्थ अलग हैं।


Example:
InCorrect - The teacher was taken back by the student's behavior.
Correct - The teacher was taken aback by the student's behavior.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
She was fond of walking along the path besides the lake.
options: besides the lake
along the path
She was
fond of walking
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "besides the lake"


Explanation:
☛ The error in the given sentence is in the phrase "besides the lake" because "besides" is incorrectly used here.
☛ "Beside" and "Besides" are two different words with distinct meanings:
- "Beside" means 'next to' or 'by the side of' (indicating location), while "Besides" means 'in addition to' (indicating something extra).
☛ In this sentence, "beside the lake" (next to the lake) is the correct usage since it describes a location.


Grammar Rules:
☛ Correct preposition selection is crucial as it changes the meaning of the sentence.
☛ "Beside" is a preposition of place, whereas "Besides" is a preposition of addition.
☛ Exams often confuse these two words, so understanding their meanings and usage is essential.


Example:
InCorrect - She sat besides me.
Correct - She sat beside me.
question_hi:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
She was fond of walking along the path besides the lake.
options_hi: besides the lake
along the path
She was
fond of walking
solution_hi:
Solution: Correct Answer is "besides the lake"


Explanation:
☛ दिए गए वाक्य में "besides the lake" में त्रुटि है क्योंकि "besides" का प्रयोग गलत है।
☛ "Beside" और "Besides" दो अलग-अलग शब्द हैं जिनके अर्थ अलग हैं।
- "Beside" का अर्थ है 'के बगल में' (पास में), जबकि "Besides" का अर्थ है 'के अलावा' (in addition to)।

Grammar Rules:

Grammar Rules:

☛ Second Conditional: If + Past Simple, would + base verb (unreal/imaginary situations).
☛ "Would" is often used for polite requests or past habits, e.g., "She would always help me."

Example:

Correct – If it rains, we will cancel the trip.

Grammar Rules:

question:

if one has the grit and determination

to keep going.
solution:
Answer: Error in part 3 – if one has the grit and determination

Error Concept: Tense consistency

The first clause uses past tense: It was possible to achieve anything.

The second clause incorrectly shifts to present tense: if one has.

Correction: It was possible to achieve anything, if one had the grit and determination to keep going.

Conclusion: The error lies in part 3 – has should be replaced with had to maintain tense consistency.

☛ Always pair time markers like 'now' with the appropriate tense (Present Continuous).

Example:

Correct - "Geeta is working now
